Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 107, English)
The Third Eye Batch: Vidya Specialization, Astral World Rules, and the Four Adhishthatri Devtas

This session opens a dedicated 1 1-day "Thir d Eye" special sadhna batch, distinct and mor e advanced/exclusive than Ashaeiynn's general teachings. It begins with a fr esh welcome, a first-time-attendee intr oduction, and its own attendance sankalp, and covers: the concept of spiritual "specialization" (vidya types), astral-world rules governing self-pr otection and mantra behavior , the speaker's own frightening astral experience fr om the pr evious night, practical rules for the 1 1-day sadhna, an extended teaching on the four adhishthatri devtas (governing subtle-body deities) illustrated thr ough Hanuman ji mythology , and a live individual checking r ound. A later portion of the same batch (mer ged in her e) adds a teaching on karma, guru-parampara, and the necessity of sustained devotion (illustrated by the Sugandha Thapa and Ankur Bhaiya stories and the purpose of Purnima Mahavan), followed by an extended, deliberately simplified teaching on how mantra ener gy works thr ough dimensions — both of or dinary space/planets and of time itself.
Part A — Opening the Third Eye Batch

1. A distinct, mor e advanced batch: The speaker opens by addressing this cohort specifically as an "1 1-day sadhna" group, noting that this Third Eye batch's content is more exclusive and advanced than Ashaeiynn's general teachings, and mentions that some devotees did not receive the previous day's recording.
2. Welcoming a first-time attendee: A first-time attendee (introduced as having a background in astrology) is welcomed to the group.
3. Framing: The speaker signals that what follows will go deeper than the standard curriculum, and that devotees should treat the material accordingly .
Part B — Spiritual "Specialization" (V idya Types)

1. Every practitioner receives one specialization, not all of them: Per this teaching, spiritual masters each receive one specific vidya (specialized ability) rather than all abilities at once — examples given include a cell-repairing/healing vidya (akin to folk/jhaada-style cures), a clairvoyance/transparency vidya, a mind-reading vidya, agni vidya (fire), ashwini vidya, and sanjeevani vidya (revival/life-restoring).

2. A specialist cannot use their own vidya on themselves: Per this teaching, a practitioner's specialization cannot be turned on themselves or (per the illustration given) even fully on their own family — illustrated through Tulsidas and Kabir , both of whom, despite their spiritual attainment, could not cure themselves or their own families through their own gifts.

3. Implication: This is presented as a structural rule of how these gifts work, not a personal failing of the practitioner — a reason why even highly attained figures still need outside help for their own or their family's problems.
Part C — Astral World Rules

1. Self-protection has no substitute — not even one's guru: Per this teaching, a devotee's own kundalini/mahasukshm sharir (great subtle body) is their sole real self-protection in the astral world; even one's own guru cannot substitute for this personal protection.

2. Pitru have no claim over a devotee's own past-life powers: Per this teaching, ancestral (pitru) spirits are connected to a devotee only through lineage and karmic debt, not through any shared claim on the devotee's own past-life powers or siddhis — pitru have no authority over abilities that belong to the devotee's own soul lineage.

3. No single mantra works identically for everyone, but some mantra works for everyone: Per this teaching, a given mantra will never produce the identical ef fect for every practitioner , though some suitable mantra exists for every person — described as a topic to be taught in more depth later in the batch.

4. Invoking past-life powers transfers contr ol of the body: Per this teaching, once a devotee invokes their kundalini/past-life powers, control over their own body ef fectively passes to those powers — this frees the devotee from many ordinary physical vulnerabilities, but requires extreme care with speech and intent, since wishes and grudges can begin to manifest almost automatically once a practitioner is immersed in this level of practice.

5. An illustration — an unintended curse that came true: The speaker recounts his own experience of an unintended curse or ill-wish manifesting as true once he was deep in this practice, of fered as a caution to take speech and intent seriously at this level.
Part D — The Speaker's Astral Experience (Pr evious Night)
1. A frightening personal astral account: The speaker shares a personal astral experience from the previous night: being sent to a realm (lok) of deceased children and grieving mothers.
2. Sent alone thr ough gatekeepers: He describes then being sent alone through gatekeeper -like elderly figures who questioned him ("what do you have?") before allowing him further .

3. A South Indian family bound to a forbidden portal: He describes arriving at a home in South India where a suf fering family (husband, wife, brother -in-law , and two small children) had built or bound an actual astral-world "door" into their bedroom wall through forbidden sadhna/sacrifice, connected to the realm of deceased children.

4. Fleeing without helping: The speaker recounts becoming frightened and leaving without of fering help, and frames this experience as a lesson on karmic debt, service obligations, and the seriousness of the practices devotees are undertaking in this batch.
Part E — Sankalp, Attendance, and Practical Sadhna Rules

1. A formal day-by-day attendance sankalp: A collective sankalp and roll call was taken for this Third Eye batch's registered devotees (summarized here rather than reproduced name-by-name, consistent with this project's convention for long roll calls), including several late-arrival name corrections read out separately .
2. Daily japa target: Devotees were instructed to begin an immediate daily tar get of four hours of japa, split into two two-hour blocks.
3. Lighting a diya per block: A diya (lamp) should be lit at the start of each two-hour block.
4. Eating r estriction: Eating is restricted to after 3 a.m. and not after 6 p.m.
5. Sleeping arrangement: Devotees should sleep on the ground, though a mattress is permitted.
6. Preparatory tilak: Devotees should apply tilak with rice, flowers, and itar (perfume) before sitting for sadhna.
7. Partner spaces and issue r eporting: Devotees were told to keep their sadhna partners' spaces adjacent to their own, and to report any issues via voice note to the admin group.
Part F — The Four Adhishthatri Devtas (Governing Subtle-Body Deities)

1. Overview: The speaker teaches that every person has four adhishthatri devtas — governing subtle-body deities — each associated with a dif ferent element and function, with kul devata (family/lineage deities) understood to sit roughly eleven levels above these four .
2. The space-element deity: The first governs all of a person's past-life powers and subtle bodies, tied to the space (akash) element.

3. The blood/flow-contr olling deity: The second is explained through medical drishti (the ability to see blood flow first), Ayurvedic vata-pitta-kapha philosophy , and cell regeneration; the speaker notes a controversial teaching attributed to this deity's tradition, which holds that physical intimacy — and not retaining "veerya" (seed) — is necessary for vitality , tying this to Patanjali's yoga sutras and the mool bandh kriya. This is presented as this tradition's own controversial claim, not as Ashaeiynn's general prescription.

4. The vayu (air/br eath)-element deity , and Hanuman ji's story: The third governs physical power and strength. The speaker illustrates this through an extended retelling of how Hanuman ji's vast ener gy was originally bound below the waist by concerned sages and his own mother , Anjana, out of fear that he was too powerful; Anjana later secretly taught him that meditation (dhyana) could redirect this ener gy upward into the brain — paralleling a "genius through breath/oxygen" idea, and distinguishing urdhagami (upward-moving) from deer ghagami (outward-moving) breath types as governing sattvik/tamasik versus rajasik tendencies. This redirection is said to have made Hanuman ji "master of masters" without needing to rely on external space-element deities.

5. The earth-element deity , and why Hanuman ji sought Sita Mata's blessing: The fourth governs magnetic/attractive force, tied to the earth (prithvi) element. The speaker recounts a second Hanuman ji mythology segment: Anjana's secret teaching that the vayu (air) and prithvi (earth) elements naturally repel one another — explaining, in this framing, why physically powerful people are often not personally magnetic or charismatic. This is given as the reason Hanuman ji deliberately sought Sita Mata's hand/blessing specifically (not only Rama's) — to acquire earth-element attractiveness and "complete" himself.
6. Closing the chapter: The speaker closes this teaching segment explicitly ("chapter closed") and assigns it as homework for devotees to reflect on.
Part G — Live Individual Checking Round

1. Overview: As with prior sessions, a live individual checking round followed the formal teaching; because it involved multiple devotees, exchanges are summarized here by theme rather than reproduced exhaustively .

2. A devotee's headache explained as a pitru "beating up" a hostile entity: One devotee's headache and anger were explained as the devotee's own pitru retaliating against a hostile outsourced entity , after the devotee's protective prayer had taken ef fect.

3. Which side pitru typically come fr om: In response to a question about whether pitru come from the mother's or father's side, the answer given was: normally the father's side, unless the mother's kul devata are the ones actively followed and worshipped in that home, in which case the mother's side becomes the operative lineage.

4. Why devotees need people/community ar ound them: An extended teaching held that pitru and past-life "soul" attachments are what draw people into a devotee's orbit and community — illustrated by references to the public mourning following the deaths of Arun Jaitley and (briefly) Dharmendra, used to show how such attachments manifest as people gathering around a person in life and in death.
Part H — A Further Day's Roll Call

1. A second day's attendance r oll call: The session (or a subsequent day within the same batch) opens with another attendance/sankalp roll call for the Third Eye batch, aggregated here rather than reproduced name-by-name.
Part I — The Gift of Time: Karma, Guru-Parampara, and the Cautionary Tale of Sugandha Thapa

1. A devotee's pr esence here is framed as completing a karmic balance: Per this teaching, a devotee's arrival in this lineage is itself the completion of a karmic balance ("karmic balance was completed there") — once that balance is complete, the devotee's path moves on elsewhere; this is of fered as the basic nature of life itself.

2. Time is not in a person's hands: Illustrated by devotees who vow to chant Ram's name "until their last breath" but pass away within a couple of years — the speaker's response ("you'll be the first to go") is used to teach that death and departure are governed by time (via the concept of the subtle body's own turning/shifting, explained earlier through "surya vigyan"), not by a person's own will or promises.

3. Nothing is simply "right" or "wrong" — situations turn: Per this teaching, a devotee who once felt af fection for the speaker and later feels aversion has not made the speaker suddenly wrong; situations shift such that things move against one or the other , and this shift itself is part of how a devotee eventually chooses to leave — "a little hatred is needed" to eventually let go and move toward the divine name alone.

4. The Sugandha Thapa story — drishti as a tool, not a possession: A devotee (Sugandha Thapa, from Lucknow) began japa, and upon the guru placing a hand on her head, her drishti (divine sight) opened immediately and she began having visions. Over time — as her circumstances shifted — she began withdrawing: she stopped addressing the speaker as "Bhaiya," stopped of fering her prayers through him, stopped treating the guru-lineage as her saakshi (witness), and eventually left the group entirely , chanting only "Jai Siyaram" independently .

5. What happens to a "tool" once its connection is dr opped: Per this teaching, drishti (the "third eye") is only a tool — "a tool by which you can see this world with an extra eye" — and once dropped without any sankalp or saakshi bhaav (witnessconsciousness) anchoring it, nearby ener gies can hijack the same tool and begin showing the practitioner whatever they want her to see, especially content that turns her against the guru lineage. When she rejoined roughly six months to a year later , she described only having "seen" negative things about the lineage during her time away .

6. Why the tool needs a guru-anchor ed channel: Per this teaching, before her withdrawal, guru-lineage shakti actively "showed" through her tool; once she stopped treating the lineage as saakshi, some other , unauthorized channel began using the same tool instead — illustrating that drishti unmoored from its original guru connection becomes vulnerable to being redirected by whichever nearby ener gy claims it.

7. The Sri Sri Ravishankar illustration — power stays only with the connected: The speaker uses a hypothetical about a wellknown spiritual figure (Sri Sri Ravishankar) to illustrate that a lar ge spiritual figure's own power is not personally "his" but

flows from the guru-lineage/shakti behind him, earned through that lineage's own ef fort and blessing; per this teaching, "whoever leaves that lineage, the powers will leave them" — a principle the speaker says applied even to himself in Ashaeiynn's early days, when devotees would say sight worked only near him and stopped when they moved away , something he could neither confirm nor deny at the time, but which he now frames as: stay connected to the guru lineage (through him or independently), and the results will follow; drift away , and they will not.

8. Purnima Mahavan (full-moon fir e ritual) — its r eal purpose: Per this teaching, no separate "special element" is extracted from the fire during Purnima Mahavan; rather , a devotee's sankalp (resolve) is of fered into the fire itself, asking to be connected to that fire's lineage — described here as the "Ram agni," with a stated boon that Gurudev will remain connected to this place for seven generations. Attending Purnima Mahavan and of fering a bhakti sankalp or jagriti sankalp there is what grants this connection.

9. What is actually being r equested at Purnima Mahavan: Per this teaching, the daily japa a devotee performs is "for themselves," but the sankalp of fered specifically at Purnima Mahavan is a bhakti sankalp — a request to remain bonded to the guru lineage and the fire's power . "Bhakti" is explained here specifically as time: gaining bhakti means gaining an ongoing extension of time and guidance from the saints/mahatmas connected to this lineage, along with an expansion of one's subtle body (sookshm sharir).

10. The Ankur Bhaiya story — devotion, prarabdha, and collective prayer: A devotee (Ankur Bhaiya) who had completed one crore (10 million) ahutis of the Ram mantra suf fered a severe accident and could not perform hawan for three months. Per this teaching, the accident itself was prarabdha (destined karma) that even the guru did not avert — but because roughly a hundred devotees prayed daily for him during that time, his own accumulated prayer -power (earned through his own ef fort) returned to him, and he was soon back sitting at hawan. The lesson given: karma/prarabdha continues to operate even for devoted practitioners, but sustained bhakti determines what support returns to a person in dif ficulty .

1 1. Devotion must be actively maintained — it does not carry over automatically: Per this teaching, if bhakti stops — even after years of intense tapasya reaching an extreme level of practice — its associated shakti departs immediately , since "if you can't even keep up the devotion itself, what will you do with the resulting power?"

12. A collective bhakti sankalp and r oll call: A formal prayer to Hanuman ji Maharaj was led, of fering japa in surrender with the speaker as saakshi, followed by a roll call of devotees who had submitted their own bhakti sankalp (aggregated here rather than reproduced name-by-name), and extended congregational bhajan/kirtan singing (including "Mere Raghav ke Darbar Mein," verses in praise of Ram, and devotional songs referencing Shabari, Krishna, and Hanuman ji).
Part J — Understanding Mantra Energy Through Dimensions

1. Chanting builds thr ough dimensional "steps" (chakras): Per this teaching, sustained mantra chanting settles progressively through dimensional steps, beginning around 14 chakras, then 32, then 64, and continuing to increase — each dimensional step functioning like a stage or gate the practitioner's ener gy crosses.

2. Mantra builds the path first, then draws the practitioner along it: Per this teaching, a mantra first builds its own "path" upward through these dimensional steps before the practitioner's kundalini shakti begins to rise and follow it; a mantra can build this path via more than one route, since chakras exist across multiple overlapping planes rather than on a single straight line, and every mantra has its own particular intensity and pace.

3. Direction is r elative to the practitioner's own position: Illustrated by a person standing on a sphere (the earth) — what looks "straight" or "crooked" depends entirely on the observer's own reference point on the curve. Per this teaching, a mantra's path is understood the same way: relative to each practitioner's own position, not an absolute, universal line.

4. Why devotees at very differ ent stages can feel the same thing: Per this teaching, because the earth (and the subtle world moving alongside it) travels a closed, looping path, two devotees traveling the same "specific path" at the same point in the loop will experience the same sensation — regardless of whether one has practiced for ten days and the other for a year and a half. This is of fered as the explanation for why newer practitioners sometimes report feelings identical to long-time practitioners'.

5. The infinity-loop shape of subtle-world motion: Per this teaching, the earth's motion together with the subtle (astral) world's parallel motion forms a closed, self-returning loop — visually resembling the infinity symbol — because a point traveling this path eventually meets itself again at the same coordinates, producing a repeating, cyclical experience rather than a simple straight ascent.

6. Kundalini shakti's coiled/serpentine appearance: Per this teaching, kundalini shakti is often perceived not as a straight line but as a coiled, DNA-helix-like or serpent-like structure, explained here as the visual result of overlapping dimensional planes rather than a single flat path.

7. Mantra travels acr oss planets, building its own path on each: Per this teaching, a devotee's mantra travels beyond the earth to other planets, crossing each planet's own dimensional planes and building its own path there — consistent with a real "parallel universe" concept, in which the same underlying work is being carried out dif ferently on each planet at once.

8. How this explains seemingly miraculous outcomes: Per this teaching, when a devotee's mantra completes its path across many planets and loops back, whatever intention was set (for example, wanting a specific outcome) is already being "worked on" in parallel across these planes; by the time this reaches the practitioner's own physical world, it appears ef fortless or miraculous, even though the underlying work took place across many dimensions. This is of fered as an explanation for how figures like Krishna performed miracles without visible personal ef fort — the necessary work was already carried out across dimensions via mantra, and Krishna himself, per this teaching, did not need to "do" anything further here.

9. Every planet (and subtle body) has a tendency to pull back toward equilibrium ("zer o"): Per this teaching, a basic principle ("a lar ger body attracts smaller bodies," compared here to a foundational science-class law) means every planet's ener gy tends to pull an aroused practitioner's mantra ener gy back down toward a resting baseline over time — described here as pointing, ultimately , toward Shiva as representing this "zero" state.

10. Why hawan (fir e ritual) matters: Per this teaching, of fering tapasya (austerity/practice) into fire removes the earth element from that of fering, which reduces this "pull-down" tendency . This is given as the reasoning behind Ashaeiynn's standing of fer: devotees who cannot personally af ford or arrange a hawan are told to continue their japa, and Ashaeiynn will fund and perform the hawan on their behalf, since the institute does not want any devotee's practice to lose ground for lack of resources.

1 1. Repetition (japa count) incr eases mantra energy , but only if devotion is sustained: Per this teaching, mantra ener gy scales roughly with repetition count (framed loosely as "one mantra times repetitions equals ener gy"), and once this ener gy is engaged through devotion, it does not fall back to zero on its own — but if the devotee's bhakti (devotion) itself lapses, the associated shakti departs immediately , since sustaining the ener gy requires sustaining the devotion that carries it.

12. Different practitioner tiers use different "stages" (charan) of japa: Per this teaching, ordinary devotees are guided through the second and third stage (charan) of japa, while saints and devtas are described as operating at the fifth and sixth stage — of fered as a reason why practitioners are deliberately not given the more advanced stages until their foundational stage is fully strong.

13. An informal mapping of dimension to spiritual attainment (offer ed as devotional framing, not literal physics): Per this teaching, the fifth dimension is associated with reaching samadhi and beginning to take on deva-like qualities; the sixth dimension with formally attaining deva status; going beyond, this framing places Kailash and Shiva around the tenth dimension, and Vaikuntha around the fourteenth — explicitly of fered by the speaker as his own simplified devotional teaching aid (referencing his own much earlier "Mool Tatva" videos on the same dimensional framework), not as a claim of rigorous
physical science. He also notes informally that some (unrelated, popular -science-style) hypotheses speculate up to around 42 dimensions, which this teaching does not adopt as its own claim.
Part K — Time Dimensions and Bringing a Vidya Into the Physical World

1. Mantra can pull events acr oss time within the same plane: Per this teaching, in the "first dimension" of time, a mantra can pull an event that was due to happen later (T2) into the present (T1), or push a present event forward, provided the event exists on the same plane.

2. A second dimension of time adds a parallel axis: Per this teaching, in a "second dimension" of time, an additional axis is introduced, allowing a mantra to draw not only forward/backward in time but also from a genuinely parallel plane running alongside the practitioner's own — described as reaching into a "parallel universe" for something not available on the practitioner's own plane.

3. Further dimensions of time access mor e parallel planes at once: Per this teaching, as this capacity increases across further dimensions, a mantra (and eventually the practitioner's own subtle body) can be simultaneously "present" across an increasing number of parallel planes at once, described as becoming steadily more omnipresent.

4. A serious caution — pulling fr om one's own timeline versus someone else's: Per this teaching, a devotee may draw needed ener gy or support from their own parallel ef forts (their own subtle body's work occurring on another plane) with comparatively little cost. However , deliberately breaking into and drawing from someone else's timeline without authorization (attributed here to tantrik practice) is described as a serious transgression: it incurs "dosha" (a spiritual debt/fault), draws intervention and a kind of cosmic "tax," and unpredictably alters both the other person's timeline and, in turn, one's own — which is why , per this teaching, the future can never be reliably or fully predicted, even with drishti.

5. Bringing a vidya fr om the astral world into the physical world: Per this teaching, manifesting any ability or outcome from the astral (subtle) world into the physical world requires making the underlying mantra work specifically within the physical dimension — described simply as moving something "from the first dimension into the second."

6. Transition into the day's checking r ound: The teaching segment closes and transitions into a live individual checking round for the day , beginning with a devotee named Deepika Joshi; this checking round was still underway and had not yet been fully shared in the source material available at the time of this Knowledge Base's writing.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

Every spiritual practitioner receives one specialization (vidya), not all gifts at once, and per this teaching cannot use that specialization to heal or help themselves or (fully) even their own family — illustrated by Tulsidas and Kabir . A devotee's own kundalini/mahasukshm sharir is their sole real self-protection in the astral world; not even a guru can substitute for it. Pitru have no claim or authority over a devotee's own past-life powers, since they are connected only by lineage and karmic debt, not shared power . No single mantra works identically for everyone, though some mantra works for every person; once kundalini/past-life powers are invoked, control of the body ef fectively passes to them, requiring great care with speech and intent since wishes and grudges can manifest almost automatically . The 1 1-day Third Eye batch's practical rules: 4 hours of daily japa split into two 2-hour blocks (each opened with a lit diya), eating only after 3 a.m. and not after 6 p.m., sleeping on the ground (mattress permitted), tilak with rice/flowers/itar before sitting, adjacent sadhna-partner spaces, and reporting issues via voice note to the admin group.

Every person has four adhishthatri devtas: a space-element deity governing past-life powers, a blood/flow-controlling deity (tied to Ayurveda and cell regeneration), a vayu-element deity governing physical strength (illustrated via Hanuman ji's originally-bound ener gy being redirected upward through Anjana's secret teaching), and an earth-element deity governing magnetism (illustrated via Hanuman ji seeking Sita Mata's blessing specifically to gain earth-element attractiveness) — with kul devata understood to sit roughly eleven levels above these four . Pitru presence normally traces to the father's side, unless the mother's kul devata are the ones actively followed in that home. Pitru and past-life "soul" attachments are taught to be what draw people/community into a devotee's orbit, in life and beyond. Drishti (the "third eye") is only a tool; the Sugandha Thapa story teaches that once a practitioner drops the guru lineage as saakshi (witness), the same tool can be redirected by other , unauthorized ener gies to show what they want shown — as illustrated by the "whoever leaves that lineage, its powers leave them" teaching. Purnima Mahavan's real purpose is of fering a bhakti sankalp (not extracting a special fire-element) to stay bonded to the guru lineage; the Ankur Bhaiya story teaches that karma/prarabdha still operates even for devoted practitioners, but sustained devotion determines what support returns to a person in dif ficulty — and that devotion must be actively maintained, since its shakti departs the moment devotion itself lapses. Mantra ener gy is taught, in this session's own deliberately simplified framework, as building a "path" through dimensional steps/chakras (first across the practitioner's own planes, then across other planets), explaining why devotees at very dif ferent stages of practice can feel identical sensations at the same point in a shared, closed ("infinity loop") path — and why hawan (which removes the earth element from an of fering) reduces the natural tendency for aroused ener gy to pull back down to baseline. In this teaching's own framework, mantra can also work across dimensions of time — pulling near -term events forward/backward on one's own plane, or (with more caution) drawing from a genuinely parallel plane; deliberately drawing from someone else's timeline without authorization is taught as a serious transgression that incurs spiritual debt and unpredictably disrupts both timelines, which is why the future can never be fully or reliably predicted, even with drishti.
